title: Prefill Deferment and Hybrid Kernel Batcher with Decode Coalescer
author: Sofia Chen
release_notes: Introduces an adaptive prefill deferment policy, a hybrid kernel batcher that consolidates single-token microbatches into kernel-sized batches, and a decode coalescer that reduces tail latency for interactive loads. Improves median tail latency and reduces token compute overhead for mixed workloads.
description: Motivation: Interactive workloads with mixed short/long requests suffer from inefficient kernel utilization and prefill/decode stage contention. The goal of this change is to reduce end-to-end latency variance while improving GPU kernel utilization for workloads that intermix single-step interactive requests and longer prefilled streams. Summary: This PR implements an adaptive prefill deferment window, a hybrid kernel batcher that opportunistically coalesces microbatches across prefills and decodes, and a decode coalescer that merges small decode handoffs into larger kernel work without violating latency SLOs. The approach preserves correctness (KV cache coherence and token ordering) and adds conservative fallbacks under high load. Key design points: 1) Prefill Deferment Policy: we introduce a time-windowed deferment heuristic that delays non-critical prefill priming for up to configurable epsilon ms when imminent decode microrequests are detected for the same session. The heuristic uses per-session score (estimated remaining tokens, decode urgency) and queue-depth signals to decide defer vs immediate prefill. 2) Hybrid Kernel Batcher: a kernel scheduler component that maintains two fast lanes: an immediate decode lane and a deferred prefill lane. When kernel occupancy is low, the batcher pulls compatible microbatches from the defer lane to reach a kernel-friendly batch size. Compatibility checks include model variant (precision/quantization), sequence-length bucket, and KV cache affinity. 3) Decode Coalescer: when multiple small decode continuations (single- or few-token advances) are pending, the coalescer rewrites kernel invocation boundaries to combine them into a single kernel call. The module enforces token ordering by constructing a merged KV mask and per-stream offsets. 4) KV Cache Hinting: prefill requests now carry a conservative 'kv-hint' (prefix priming score) used by the batcher to avoid evicting primed keys that will be reused within the deferred window. Hints are advisory and do not change cache eviction semantics under memory pressure. 5) Fallbacks & Safety: if the hybrid batcher detects incompatible requests (different quantization or model variant), it falls back to prior scheduling. Also added diagnostic counters and tracing for per-request decision provenance. Commits summary: - Add prefill deferment policy and configuration knobs (prefill/defer/*) - Implement kernel batcher with compatibility checks and lane arbitration - Add decode coalescer that merges small decodes into coalesced kernels - Propagate kv-hint metadata through request routing and scheduler - Add unit and integration tests covering ordering and KV coherence - Add perf bench harness and benchmark results collection - Instrumentation: metrics, trace events, and per-request decision tags Changed files (high-level): runtime/scheduler/hybrid_batcher.cc runtime/scheduler/hybrid_batcher.h runtime/scheduler/prefill_defer_policy.cc runtime/scheduler/prefill_defer_policy.h runtime/kvcache/kv_hinting.cc runtime/kvcache/kv_hinting.h runtime/decoder/decode_coalescer.cc runtime/decoder/decode_coalescer.h runtime/telemetry/decision_tags.cc runtime/tests/test_prefill_defer.cc runtime/tests/test_decode_coalesce.cc perf/benchmarks/prefill_decode_coalesce_bench.py docs/perf/prefill-deferment.md docs/architecture/prefill-batcher.md Why this is different from prior work: rather than only increasing prefetch aggressiveness or purely changing prefill granularity, this patch adds a time-aware deferment layer and couples it with a kernel-level opportunistic batcher that respects model/kernel compatibility. The decode coalescer focuses on the runtime handoff semantics rather than model-level changes. Performance results (internal perf/bench runs): - Interactive median latency: -3.4% (vs main baseline) - 95th percentile latency: -12.8% on mixed short/long workload (simulated conversational traffic) - Token GPU compute per-request: -9.5% (due to fewer small kernel invocations) - Throughput at 99% latency budget: +8% on mixed workload Notes on measurement: Benchmarks run on p4d-equivalent profile with sequence-length distribution approximating 60% short (<=16 tokens), 40% long. We include both cold-start (empty KV) and warm-start scenarios. Review thread (highlights): Marco Liu (reviewer): "Nice design; two immediate asks: 1) ensure the hint does not hide correctness bugs when eviction occurs; add a debug mode that forces eviction path during tests; 2) microbench the extra decision latency in the scheduler." Sofia Chen (author): "Added forced-eviction test and microbench in perf harness; decision path added ~120ns median on hot path, see perf results summary." Asha Patel (reviewer): "Can we expose the defer window as a per-deployment config? Also request a short doc section describing safe knob ranges." Sofia Chen: "Defer window is configurable via runtime.json and the docs page includes recommended ranges (5-40ms) and tradeoffs." Riley Thompson (reviewer): "Please ensure the coalescer does not increase tail latency under heavy contention." Sofia Chen: "Added a protective watermark: coalescing is disabled when decode queue depth > 0.6 * max_decode_queue or when kernel latency exceeds historical threshold." CI and gating: All unit tests and integration tests passed on CI. Perf bench compared patch vs main across 10 runs; aggregated results above. Post-merge actions: - Rollout gated behind a feature flag (runtime.config.enable_prefill_defer=true) - Monitoring: added metrics: scheduler.defer_attempts, scheduler.defer_success, batcher.coalesced_kernels, kvcache.hint_hits - Run gradual canary across 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic with alerting on 95p latency regression >5% Known limitations and future work: - Current compatibility checks treat different quantization modes as incompatible; future work could support on-the-fly kernel selection for mixed-precision coalescing. - The kv-hint is advisory and can be extended to inform soft-eviction policies when memory pressure is predictable. - More thorough multi-tenant tests are planned. Infra/ops notes: Feature gated; no DB migrations. Backwards compatibility preserved for existing clients. A follow-up PR will expose telemetry in the Console and add a per-model recommended defer profile.
